title: I dug into how the top Solana memecoin traders actually make $30k/month. It's not skill — and it changes how you should code your entry filter.
author: paulf280
selftext: Spent the week pulling on-chain data and reading the forensics (Pine Analytics, Bloomberg's cabal reporting, etc.). The uncomfortable conclusion: the leaderboard "geniuses" aren't out-trading anyone. **Over half of** [**pump.fun**](http://pump.fun) **tokens are sniped in the** ***creation block*** **by wallets the deployer funded** — they bundle their own buy at the bottom, manufacture a clean-looking distribution across 20+ fresh wallets, let retail and copy-bots chase it up, then dump. **87% of those creation-block snipes are profitable** — a win rate that's only possible if you already know the launch is coming, because you're running it. The practical takeaway for anyone building a trading agent: **don't try to copy the winners (their wallets are disposable and already exited — you become exit liquidity), and don't chase speed. Filter.** The edge a small trader can actually hold is avoiding the launches that are engineered to dump on you. I ended up building that filter into a tool — it gives one verdict per mint: *are insiders positioned to dump on you?* (bundled launch, single-wallet concentration, shared-funder cluster, serial-rug dev). Free, no signup, and every flag links to the on-chain tx so you can verify instead of trusting a score. Happy to share the link in a comment if useful — mainly posting because the "the leaderboard is mostly insiders" finding genuinely changed how I think about entries.

comments.body:
As someone who spends a lot of time building and reviewing software, I don't often come across projects that genuinely catch my attention.

While browsing GitHub today, I stumbled across a repository called **zipsey** a Telegram based Solana memecoin trading platform.

What stood out wasn't just the trading features, but how much functionality has been packed into a single Telegram interface. It combines real-time market intelligence, automated trading, wallet management, portfolio tracking, and risk management into one streamlined experience.

The architecture is surprisingly well organized, and it feels like much more than a typical Telegram bot. It looks like the developer has put a lot of thought into both usability and scalability.

Definitely an interesting project if you're into Solana, Telegram bots, or automated trading.

🔗 *GitHub Repository:* [https://github.com/zipseysol/Zipsey---Your-Automated-Trading-Agent.git](https://github.com/zipseysol/Zipsey---Your-Automated-Trading-Agent.git)
